title: Phenylalanine Hydroxylase Deficiency
result: Expert-authored, peer-reviewed chapter, first posted 2000, comprehensive update 13 March 2025, revised 20 November 2025. Autosomal recessive; biallelic PAH variants; PAH at 12q23.2. Phenylketonuria denotes untreated plasma phenylalanine above 1,000 umol/L; untreated or late-diagnosed disease causes irreversible intellectual disability, seizures and microcephaly. Defects of tetrahydrobiopterin synthesis or recycling (GCH1, PTS, QDPR, PCBD1) account for about 2% of raised blood phenylalanine. Newborn screening uses dried blood spots collected 24 to 72 hours after birth, with phenylalanine and tyrosine measured by tandem mass spectrometry; biochemical diagnosis requires blood phenylalanine above 120 umol/L and a phenylalanine-to-tyrosine ratio of 3 or more. Treatment: phenylalanine-restricted diet with phenylalanine-free protein supplements based on amino acids or glycomacropeptide; 25% to 50% respond to sapropterin, a synthetic form of tetrahydrobiopterin; pegvaliase, a PEGylated phenylalanine ammonia lyase given subcutaneously, is approved in the US for adults with phenylalanine above 600 umol/L. Aspartame is metabolised in the gut to phenylalanine and aspartate. Maternal phenylalanine consistently above 360 umol/L in pregnancy causes intellectual disability in more than 90% of offspring. The chapter attributes brain toxicity to phenylacetic, phenylpyruvic and phenyllactic acids and to tyrosine and neurotransmitter deficiency.
